findings.claim: Typical factors of safety: bridges and cranes (FoS 4–6), aircraft structures (FoS 1.5–2, minimised to reduce weight), lifting equipment (FoS 6–10 by regulation).
findings.truth: There is no universal factor-of-safety range for these applications. The appropriate value depends on the application, its risks and the relevant standard.
findings.evidence: HSE LOLER overview (fetched): lifting equipment must have adequate strength and stability, and the risk assessment and planning must reflect the operation.

findings.claim: A Charpy test piece is gripped horizontally.
findings.truth: A Charpy specimen is supported at its two ends on an anvil before the pendulum strikes it.
findings.evidence: TWI, What is a Charpy Impact Test? (fetched).

findings.claim: Dye penetrant testing detects surface-breaking cracks in non-magnetic materials.
findings.truth: Liquid penetrant testing is suitable for clean, non-porous materials, including both magnetic and non-magnetic metals.
findings.evidence: TWI, What is Liquid Penetrant Testing? (fetched).

findings.claim: The matching answer restricts dye penetrant testing to non-magnetic materials.
findings.truth: The material condition is clean and non-porous, not non-magnetic.
findings.evidence: TWI, What is Liquid Penetrant Testing? (fetched).

findings.claim: Hardness testing is presented as categorically destructive.
findings.truth: TWI lists hardness testing among destructive laboratory tests, while ASTM notes that indentation hardness testing can be non-destructive when the part remains usable. Either retain the laboratory-sample convention or revise all affected references to say that classification depends on serviceability.
findings.evidence: TWI, Materials Testing Laboratories and Services; ASTM STP24011S, Factors That Affect the Accuracy of Indentation Hardness Tests (both fetched).

findings.claim: An isometric drawing has all three principal axes at 30° to the horizontal.
findings.truth: In an isometric drawing, vertical lines are vertical and the two horizontal axes are at 30° to the horizontal.

findings.claim: The flashcard says all three isometric axes are at 30°.
findings.truth: Only the two horizontal isometric axes are at 30°; the vertical axis remains vertical.

findings.claim: CAM converts CAD geometry directly into G-code with no manual programming required.
findings.truth: CAM uses selected manufacturing settings to create toolpaths; a post-processor converts those toolpaths into machine-specific code. Manual G-code writing can be reduced, but CAM still needs setup and toolpath choices.
findings.evidence: Autodesk Fusion CAM documentation on toolpaths and post-processing (fetched).

findings.claim: The CAM practice answer says CAM removes the need for manual programming.
findings.truth: CAM creates toolpaths from CAD geometry and selected settings, then post-processes them into machine instructions; it does not remove the need to set up the machining operations.
findings.evidence: Autodesk Fusion CAM documentation on toolpaths and post-processing (fetched).

summary: Four lessons checked. Eight verified, surgical corrections are supplied; the classification of indentation hardness testing needs an editorial decision.
